vaccinations.name: DTaP-HB-IPV-Hib (Infanrix hexa)
vaccinations.description: Protects against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (whooping cough), hepatitis B, polio, and Haemophilus influenzae type b. First dose at 2 months.

vaccinations.name: DTaP-HB-IPV-Hib (Infanrix hexa)
vaccinations.description: Second dose of the 6-in-1 vaccine at 4 months.

vaccinations.name: DTaP-HB-IPV-Hib (Infanrix hexa)
vaccinations.description: Third dose of the 6-in-1 vaccine at 6 months.

vaccinations.name: Pneumococcal Conjugate (Pneu-C-13 or Synflorix)
vaccinations.description: Protects against pneumococcal disease (pneumonia, meningitis, blood infections). First dose at 2 months.

vaccinations.name: Pneumococcal Conjugate (Pneu-C-13 or Synflorix)
vaccinations.description: Second dose of pneumococcal vaccine at 4 months.

vaccinations.name: Rotavirus (Rotarix or RotaTeq)
vaccinations.description: Oral vaccine that protects against rotavirus, a common cause of severe diarrhea. First dose at 2 months.
vaccinations.notes: Oral vaccine, not an injection. Must be completed by 8 months of age.

vaccinations.name: Rotavirus (Rotarix or RotaTeq)
vaccinations.description: Second and final dose of rotavirus oral vaccine at 4 months.
vaccinations.notes: Oral vaccine, not an injection. Final dose.

vaccinations.name: Meningococcal C Conjugate (Men-C-C)
vaccinations.description: Protects against meningococcal C disease (meningitis and blood infections). Given at 12 months.

vaccinations.name: Pneumococcal Conjugate (Pneu-C-13 or Synflorix)
vaccinations.description: Third and final dose of pneumococcal vaccine at 12 months.

vaccinations.name: MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella)
vaccinations.description: Protects against measles, mumps, and rubella. First dose at 12 months.

vaccinations.name: Varicella (Chickenpox)
vaccinations.description: Protects against chickenpox (varicella). First dose at 12 months.

vaccinations.name: DTaP-IPV-Hib
vaccinations.description: Booster dose of diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, and Hib vaccines at 18 months.

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A
vaccinations.description: Protects against hepatitis A. First dose at 24 months (2 years).
vaccinations.notes: Not universally funded in BC, but recommended for high-risk groups

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A
vaccinations.description: Second dose of hepatitis A vaccine, given 6 months after first dose.
vaccinations.notes: Not universally funded in BC, but recommended for high-risk groups

vaccinations.name: DTaP-IPV (Tdap-IPV)
vaccinations.description: Kindergarten booster for diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, and polio at 4-6 years.

vaccinations.name: MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella)
vaccinations.description: Second dose of MMR vaccine at 4-6 years (kindergarten).

vaccinations.name: Varicella (Chickenpox)
vaccinations.description: Second dose of varicella vaccine at 4-6 years (kindergarten).

vaccinations.name: Tdap (Tetanus, Diphtheria, Pertussis)
vaccinations.description: Grade 9 booster for tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis at age 14-15 years.

vaccinations.name: Meningococcal ACYW-135 Conjugate
vaccinations.description: Grade 9 vaccine protecting against meningococcal disease types A, C, Y, and W-135.

vaccinations.name: HPV9 (Human Papillomavirus)
vaccinations.description: Grade 6 vaccine (age 11-12) protecting against 9 types of HPV that cause cancer and genital warts.

vaccinations.name: HPV9 (Human Papillomavirus)
vaccinations.description: Second dose of HPV vaccine, given 6 months after first dose.

vaccinations.name: Influenza (Flu) - Annual
vaccinations.description: Annual flu vaccine recommended starting at 6 months of age. Protects against seasonal influenza.
vaccinations.notes: Annual vaccination recommended every fall. First-time recipients under 9 years need 2 doses, 4 weeks apart.

notes: This schedule follows the BC Immunization Schedule for 2024
Some vaccines may be combined into single injections
Talk to your healthcare provider about catch-up schedules if doses are missed
High-risk groups may require additional vaccinations
Premature infants follow the same schedule based on chronological age
Consult your healthcare provider for specific recommendations
